I am 70 years old now, and I have been farming this same 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 20 years. I only finished primary school, so I do not read farming books. I watch what works. My neighbor Lao Zhang got good wheat last year with the improved Jimai variety, so I will buy that seed again — about 15 jin per mu when I sow in October. For the summer maize, I use hybrid seed from the county dealer, about 3 jin per mu. I saw it grow tall and strong on my field last year, so I trust it.

For fertilizer, I always start from what I did last year because change is risky. Before wheat sowing, I spread one 50-kilogram bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer on each mu. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I topdress with 20 kilograms of urea per mu. That gives me about 17 kilograms of nitrogen, 7.5 kilograms of phosphorus, and 7.5 kilograms of potassium per mu. The compound bag costs about 160 yuan now and urea is 120 yuan, so it is not cheap, but a bad harvest is a disaster and wasting a little fertilizer is only money down the drain. For the maize after wheat harvest, I put 40 kilograms of compound per mu at planting, and 15 kilograms of urea when the plants are knee-high. That is about 13 kilograms of nitrogen, 6 kilograms of phosphorus, and 6 kilograms of potassium per mu.

I have my well, so I water the wheat three times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing in March, and once when the heads come out. The maize I water twice — right after sowing if June is dry, and at the big trumpet stage in July. My well pump uses electricity, about 30 yuan each time for the whole field. For chemicals, I spray the wheat twice: herbicide when the weeds are small, and fungicide when I see yellow spots on the leaves. The maize gets two sprays: herbicide after emergence, and insecticide when the worms come in July. I hire the crop-dusting drone from the village cooperative — 8 yuan per mu each time — because my back cannot carry a heavy tank anymore. For tillage, I hire the rotary tiller from the machinery team for both crops, 40 yuan per mu. It is fast and does a fine job. I expect about 550 kilograms of wheat per mu and 650 kilograms of maize per mu if the weather holds. Last year dry wind in May hurt me a little, so this year I hope for better.
